brief: Goldman FICC's macro roadmap runs five threads. Persian Gulf exports at 15-16mb/day, two thirds of pre-war, plus dark transits and elastic China buying have capped crude, but European gas and diesel are stressed, so front end UK and European rates now track gas more than crude, and the open question is whether product stress feeds core inflation. From here the sharp move is skewed lower on a positive headline against a grind higher on no news. Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole speech lowered the CPI bar for a September hike, Waller pushed back and will vote hold absent a hot print, ticking that bar back up, so next week's CPI decides. A 0.2bp MoM core print should be enough to hold, a close call, and any cycle is judged shallow. Long end weakness is structural: large deficits plus shrinking duration demand mean buybacks, WAM cuts and hikes flatten curves without solving it, so European long end is a short and steepeners are bullish duration. ECB September 25bp is locked with terminal pricing at 3%. BoE modal case stays on hold, pivot risk rising with gas.
